schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE A (A1 INT, A2 INT);
CREATE TABLE B (B1 INT, B2 INT);
q1: SELECT X.A1 AS A1, X.A2 AS A2, Y.B1 AS B1, Y.B2 AS B2 FROM A AS X, B AS Y WHERE X.A1 = Y.B1
q2: SELECT Y.A1 AS A1, Y.A2 AS A2, X.B1 AS B1, X.B2 AS B2 FROM B AS X, A AS Y WHERE Y.A1 = X.B1
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT X.A1 AS A1, X.A2 AS A2, Y.B1 AS B1, Y.B2 AS B2 FROM A AS X, B AS Y WHERE X.A1 = Y.B1
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT Y.A1 AS A1, Y.A2 AS A2, X.B1 AS B1, X.B2 AS B2 FROM B AS X, A AS Y WHERE Y.A1 = X.B1
counterexample:
INSERT INTO A (A1, A2) VALUES (1, 10);
INSERT INTO B (B1, B2) VALUES (1, 20);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. Q1 joins table A (aliased as X) with table B (aliased as Y) on X.A1 = Y.B1 and selects columns A1, A2 from A and B1, B2 from B. Q2 joins table B (aliased as X) with table A (aliased as Y) on Y.A1 = X.B1 and selects columns A1, A2 from A (aliased as Y) and B1, B2 from B (aliased as X). The column aliases differ, so the output columns are swapped in order and potentially in meaning.
counterexample_dsp: Insert a row into A with A1 = 1 and A2 = 10, and a row into B with B1 = 1 and B2 = 20. Q1 will return (1, 10, 1, 20) while Q2 will return (1, 20, 1, 10).
